boundary: Programmable secure container sandbox service for running untrusted or generated code with resource, timeout, networking and snapshot controls; it is infrastructure, not an app-builder UX.
workflows: Create a sandbox with an image/app, execute code or services, expose readiness/tunnels when configured, terminate on completion/timeout, and snapshot/restore filesystem or memory state.
prompting_planning: No product-level natural-language planning or generated-app workflow is established.
generated_artifacts: Sandbox filesystem, processes, logs, snapshots and mounted volumes are documented; application artifact schema and provenance are caller-owned/unknown.
data_auth_integration: Volumes, tunnels and Modal resources are available through explicit configuration; credential isolation and external data connectors are unknown.
ui_design: No UI design-generation surface is established.
runtime_sandbox: Secure-by-default sandboxing, configurable CPU/memory/timeouts, no inbound network by default and outbound block/allowlist controls are documented.
deploy_export: Services can use tunnels; sandbox image/snapshot portability and infrastructure export semantics are unknown.
collaboration: Shared volumes and snapshot branching support technical collaboration; user-level review/approval is unknown.
recovery: Filesystem, directory and memory snapshots restore state, with TTL and process/connection limitations; external side effects and complete recovery receipts are unknown.
governance_security: Network controls and resource limits are documented; tenant isolation, audit retention, compliance and incident details are unknown.

contradictions: Snapshotting preserves state but terminates the sandbox and does not restore open TCP connections/background processes; snapshot is not equivalent to transparent live checkpointing.

boundary: Programmable composable computer/sandbox infrastructure for AI agents with container, Linux VM, Windows and GPU variants; not a user-facing application builder.
workflows: Create isolated sandboxes, use filesystem/Git/process/computer-use APIs, persist via stop/start or snapshots, fork VM state, mount shared volumes and scale one sandbox per task/agent.
prompting_planning: Agent execution environment is documented, but product-level prompt planning/checkpoint semantics are unknown.
generated_artifacts: Filesystem, Git repositories, processes, snapshots, forks, logs and volume data are documented; application schema/provenance are caller-owned.

ui_design: No design-generation surface is established, though computer-use access is documented.
runtime_sandbox: Dedicated kernel/filesystem/network stack and allocated resources per sandbox are documented; container/VM/GPU classes and network policy are documented at boundary level.
deploy_export: Snapshots, OCI images, Git operations and volumes provide infrastructure primitives; deployment export and portability across providers are unknown.
collaboration: Shared volumes, linked sandboxes and Git operations support multi-agent/task workflows; human review/approval is unknown.
recovery: Stop/start preserves filesystem, snapshots preserve state, VM pause/resume and fork preserve memory; linked sandboxes are ephemeral and cannot resume after stop.
governance_security: Per-sandbox isolation, limits, enterprise SSO/audit/BYOC signals and per-tenant volume subpaths are documented; full compliance/retention model is unknown.
economics: Pay-as-you-go resource billing per second and resource-specific prices are documented; exact enterprise discounts and export cost are unknown.
contradictions: Persistence is class-dependent: containers preserve filesystem but not memory on stop, VM pause can preserve memory, and linked children are explicitly ephemeral.
Volume sharing enables collaboration but concurrent writes are non-transactional and last-write-wins.
